title: Adjoint of the unbounded proper-open refinement comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $U,V_1,V_2$ be Noetherian schemes, meaning schemes with finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $p:V_1\to V_2$ be proper and let $j_i:U\hookrightarrow V_i$ be open immersions with $pj_1=j_2$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For the commutative square with top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, left edge $1_U$ and right edge $p$, let
$$b_p:Dj_{2!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*Dj_{1!}$$
be the specific proper/open comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], normalized on a K-injective complex $J$ on $U$ and a K-injective resolution $j_{1!}J\to I$ by $j_{2!}J\cong p_*j_{1!}J\to p_*I$. Here $Dj_{i!}$ means degreewise exact extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Write $\varepsilon_p:p^*Rp_*\to1$ for the counit of exact inverse image and derived direct image [def-kun-unbounded-exchange].
For a module sheaf $M$ on $U$, let $\pi_{p,M}:p^*j_{2!}M\to j_{1!}M$ be the following sheaf map. Put $W=p^{-1}(j_2(U))$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $j_1:U\to W$ is a clopen section of $W\to U$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen]. Under open-extension base change [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], $p^*j_{2!}M$ is extension by zero from $W$ of the pullback of $M$. Define $\pi_{p,M}$ to be its projection onto the component $j_1(U)$, identity there and zero on its complement, using the sheaf decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product]. The construction is natural in $M$ and descends degreewise to $D\pi_p:p^*Dj_{2!}\to Dj_{1!}$. Then the equality of natural transformations on all unbounded complexes is
$$\varepsilon_{p,Dj_{1!}(-)}\circ p^*b_p=D\pi_p.$$
No cartesian condition on the displayed refinement square is assumed.

proof.text: First specialize the sheaf and representative normalizations of lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange at (j1,id,p,j2), retaining them in ProperOpenRefinementData. The named existence theorem is proved from that interchange. Both comparison maps are determined by their normalization formulas; the structure avoids repeated kernel reduction of the full global existential. Insert lowerStarId into its sheaf comparison and take the ordinary p-adjoint to obtain the natural sheaf map pi. The normalization into the common direct image, the formula for upperStarComp as conjugation of lowerStarComp, and the two open-unit identities give the displayed section formula for j1* pi. For each disjoint open c, c* j1! M is zero by the existing open-extension complement API, so c* pi is zero. These are exactly the two component formulas in the statement.

Descend the degreewise natural transformation pi using Localization.liftNatTrans. Compose with the inverse exact derived composition isomorphism. The liftNatTrans component formula and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac give exactly the displayed equality on every cochain complex J. The public exact identity factorization of lem-pur-exact-restriction-composition identifies the identity direct-image compositor on representatives.

At a K-injective J, choose a K-injective resolution rho of j1! J. The representative normalization in lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange, after inserting and cancelling the identity direct-image normalization, expresses the refinement comparison as Q(theta_J) followed by Q(p_*rho). Apply p* and use lem-asd-derived-counit-k-injective-termwise to express the derived counit at QI as the ordinary degreewise counit with the exact factorization. Naturality of the derived counit along the localization of rho, then naturality of the ordinary counit along rho, reduces the composite to Q(pi_J) followed by Q(rho). Cancel the factorization and Q(rho), both isomorphisms. Every derived object is isomorphic to QJ for K-injective J; naturality transports the equality to all objects, giving equality of the natural transformations.
